video_title: Luka Makes MVP Case! + Heat, Knicks & Warriors Still WINLESS!

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic is putting the Lakers in a great position
quotes.excerpt: Luka has done a great job of putting the Lakers in a great position to start the season.
quotes.quote: I think he's off to a great start. With everything being said in the off-season, people saying that this team isn't going to be competitive, they're too whatever, whatever. LeBron James' exit, they've responded. A lot of that has to do with Luka from rattling the cage of a rookie to start this season to just what he's been able to do to going off for 52 and putting himself at the head of this MVP conversation. I think he's done a great job of putting the Lakers in a great position to start this season. DeMarcus Cousins can attest to this, the schedule has been favorable for the Lakers to start the season. You win the games that on paper you're supposed to win against those matchups and they've been able to do that. At some point the schedule is going to get serious, it's going to get real. I want to see how they stand in the Western Conference when they start running into some of the teams that's at the top of the food chain like they are.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic is the engine of the Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: This is Luka's team now, this is exactly what he wanted and this is the position he wanted.
quotes.quote: Part of your job as a professional is to beat the teams you're supposed to beat. Regardless of the strength of schedule, regardless of the opponent, the Lakers are 3-0 right now and they're doing their job. There's been a lot of knocks and displeasure with what the team looks like since LeBron's departure, but this is Luka's team now, this is exactly what he wanted and this is the position he wanted. As of now, he's doing everything he's supposed to do. He's the head of the snake, he's the engine in the car and he's leading this team right now. Incredible performance last night. He's now put his name in that hat for MVP candidate this season and if you disagree, at this point you're just hating. The guy is the real deal, he's shown it year in, year out. He's starting the season off hot, so let's keep it rolling.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Giannis and Bam duo needs to improve their chemistry
quotes.excerpt: The biggest hole in their offense as of right now to me is figuring out that big, big dynamic.
quotes.quote: It's more so just figuring out chemistry, figuring out how to play next to one another. The biggest hole in their offense as of right now to me is figuring out that big, big dynamic. I've spoken on it in the past and I got a lot of heat from Miami Heat fans as far as comparing. The reason I compared in the first place was because this is the same issue that me and Anthony Davis ran into when we teamed up. The difference is I got traded halfway through the year, so we had that half a year after All-Star break to kind of work through our mistakes and our kinks. But going into the off-season, we used that small example of things that didn't work, what we needed to correct and what we needed to work on, and we took that over into the brand new season. With Miami, they didn't really get that luxury. They're learning everything on the fly and they're also learning in front of everybody. As of right now, I just don't see that dynamic working. They have to figure out how to play with one another, figure out that space and figuring out how to both be aggressive within that dynamic.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Heat need a playmaker to help Giannis and Bam
quotes.excerpt: You need somebody that's going to be a playmaker. He's making open shots, he's creating shots for himself.
quotes.quote: A playmaker is a good call, somebody that can make plays. I've been seeing some stuff where they're just talking about a point guard. Davion Mitchell is doing his job, he's averaging 17 and 8 right now. But you need somebody that's going to be a playmaker. He's making open shots, he's creating shots for himself, but he's got to have somebody, they've got to have somebody on the floor that's going to draw some attention, that's going to open up some driving lanes for Bam and Giannis. For me, my issue with the Miami Heat right now, it looks like they're still trying to find an identity. One game they shoot 53s, the next game they're shooting 33s. Teams are packing in the paint, they don't have an identity. Bam and Giannis, they kind of operate in the same areas on the floor. They both like to catch it at like that mid-post area, that free throw line area and they create from there. If you got two guys that love to play in the same spots, it's kind of difficult. Every clip that we just showed, you saw five guys packing the paint every time one of these guys got the basketball or they're trying to drive to the to the lane, they're going to make it difficult for this team to score points.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Bam Adebayo needs to play with more aggression
quotes.excerpt: I need Bam to be the most aggressive version of himself for this to work.
quotes.quote: It's all chatter and talk and let me say this before I say anything, I'm a huge fan of Bam. I've been a fan of Bam since he came to Kentucky. Huge supporter of myself, but everything Kevin Garnett is saying is correct. I said it at the beginning of the year when this tandem came together, but we need Bam to be the most aggressive version of himself for this to work. Playing hesitant, thinking with every catch, we just need you to be in go mode. That was one thing that me and Anthony Davis had to figure out because a lot of the times we would hold back and it would not only harm us as individuals but it would also harm the team. I see a lot of hesitation in Bam's game. I just need him to be the most aggressive version of himself in order to make this tandem work. He's also going to have to figure out that three-ball situation. In the past, I see him shooting two to three maybe in a game, I said before that number is going to have to go up. We're going to need about five, six to maybe even seven threes a game from him for this offense to have some type of flow, some type of space and then just some type of chemistry within it.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo need to find a way to coexist
quotes.excerpt: They just got to figure out a way to coexist. Neither one of those guys are playmakers.
quotes.quote: We can say everything about Giannis, this and that, but at the end of the day, none of these guys were here last year with Bam and he was doing just fine. They just got to figure out a way to coexist. Neither one of those guys are playmakers. They're going to need somebody on the floor to set the table for them. When Bam was by himself, it was a little different because he was the guy with the ball in his hands. He didn't need anybody to make the plays for him because he had the ball. When you bring a Giannis in, the ball is obviously going to be in Giannis's hand, right? And he's not necessarily a playmaker that he can go out there, they can play a two-man where, you know, Giannis has the ball in his hands, Bam is screening for him or rolling or putting they're putting pressure on the rim, whether they're getting down hill, two-on-one and creating opportunities for themselves. It's just, listen, when they go in the pick-and-roll with each other, teams are just packing the paint right now. So they got to figure out a way to get more stops, to play more freely that way both of those guys can look like their natural selves.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks are struggling because teams know their style of play
quotes.excerpt: They got a certain style of play that everybody was able to watch. You're on the biggest stage.
quotes.quote: Listen, they got a certain style of play that everybody was able to watch. You're on the biggest stage. So while you guys were competing for a championship, the rest of the league was at home watching you guys and studying you guys. You became a marked target for what teams and players individually wanted to accomplish. And so when you come back into that season and you bring everybody back, you still have that same style of play, you haven't tweaked a lot of things. Teams have been able to scout it way more than you've been able to scout them and they've had success with competing against you. That's part of the hangover. It's not necessarily saying that the Knicks are going to come into the season and not take the opportunity serious to go back-to-back and try to repeat. No, it's just the odds are stacked against you because everybody understands your style of play. Everybody knows what you're bringing to the table. It was somewhat of a surprise for us last year that they got to the championship. Now it's not. You're the top dog. There's no more surprises. We know who's who's going to have the ball in the fourth quarter. We know that Josh Hart and Bridges are going to be the energy guys and I know that and I'm just on TV. So the guys that's competing against them, they understand what it takes to be able to try to go out and beat this basketball team.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks are in a tough spot after a slow start
quotes.excerpt: I think it's a lot of season left, I think it's plenty of time to turn this around.
quotes.quote: You made a point as far as this team, you know, starting off slow. So they they do have a history of kind of having ups and downs throughout their season but they've also also shown that they can go run off 10 straight at any moment. So I think this is kind of a part of their identity. It's almost like they got to kind of get put in the corner first to then press the gas and and move forward. So I think this is a lot of season left, I think it's plenty of time to turn this around obviously, but I don't think we've seen the best version of the Knicks this season. It could be, you know, the off-season playing a part in it. It could also be the contract extension talks that's that's kind of been put at a halt. And I also feel like, you know, James Dolan had a pretty loud message without saying anything as far as not extending the guys, not really improving the team over in the off-season. It seems like they are a little content with just winning one. You know what I mean? So, and and, Lou, you know as a player when it comes to setting the tone within an organization, starts at the top. Starts at the top. So I think James Dolan's message has been pretty clear and loud as far as being content with just winning one. So I don't want to look into it too much, but I think that's that's that could be a real thing for this group.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Warriors are in a difficult situation without Jimmy Butler
quotes.excerpt: This is a storybook ending that's coming to a close with Steve Kerr, Draymond and Steph.
quotes.quote: To me, it looks like this is a storybook ending that's coming to a close with Steve Kerr, Draymond and Steph and what they can do in the Western Conference as a collective. They got a lot of young guys around and the veterans that they do have, they over the hump of being old guys. And I'm trying to say that in the most respectful way possible because I I have so much love and admiration for Steph, for Dray, for Al Horford. But all of those guys are over the hump when it comes to the age and now you have, you know, some young guys that you kind of start shifting to, let's start building around them. Like Draymond said, I think we found a new face of the franchise. When you start talking like that, that means that there's a passing of the baton and we're going in a different direction and we understand that we're going to be going in a different direction, uh, sooner sooner than we probably expected or or or they're right on they're right on schedule as far as everything that they've expected this group to be. But to be 0-3, it's just it's it's going to be tough, man. I want to root for this team, I want to root for Steph, he's he's been a pillar in our game. I want to root for those guys but I but, you know, it's obvious that as a collective as a whole that their best days are behind them.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Warriors' front office is living in the past
quotes.excerpt: I think the front office is is still living like off nostalgia, like they were great 10 years ago.
quotes.quote: I think Steph has so much more greatness to give even at this point in his career. I just don't I don't feel like the front office is is believing in Steph the way everybody in the world believes in Steph and and I think the evidence is pretty apparent. I I'll go on the record and say I think James Dolan has done a shit job as far as putting the roster around Steph Curry. Why this guy still has a job, I'll never know. Obviously, I don't have that privilege in life. So I think he's done a horrible job as far as putting a good group around him. They're still running the same outdated system as far as going extremely small. I think I think last the other nights Steve Kerr put in a lineup and the tallest guy on the floor was 6-6. It just doesn't work, it doesn't work anymore. The system is outdated. Even the iPhone updates every couple of months. Like let's be real here. So it it sucks to see Steph kind of go out on his limb like I said, I feel like he has a lot more greatness to give, same goes for Draymond. I'm a huge fan of the root y'all, I think he's going to have an incredible career. I love his confidence, I love his mentality, I love everything he brings to the game. I am concerned about the development and it's not because of him, but because of the history of the people around him.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Warriors are in a gray area with their roster
quotes.excerpt: I think Golden State is in a gray area. They showed you that by Steve Kerr getting his deal.
quotes.quote: I think Golden State is in a gray area. They showed you that by Steve Kerr getting his deal, by Steph Curry getting two more years, by Draymond coming back. We're in a gray area. Listen, we're going to ride this thing out to the sunset. We we've built something from ground up, we put the foundation in, we got a lot of success out of it. We at the end of the road with with this particular group right here. Let's start going to find some young pieces to kind of mesh and mold into that and then we're going to phase this thing out and we're going to start going in a different direction. And at the same time, there's still dealing with one of their best players being out of the lineup until Christmas or or or some something like that when it comes to Jimmy. I think that team is is going to look better than it is. I don't think this team is built to compete for a championship, but I think they're better than the 0-3 start. I could be wrong.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Yaxel is not afraid of Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: I'm not afraid to talk to nobody. He's not Michael Jordan.
quotes.quote: I'm not afraid to talk to nobody. He's not Michael Jordan.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I'm not afraid to talk to nobody. He's not Michael Jordan.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum is a top-50 player of all time
quotes.excerpt: Scottie Pippen is a top-50 player of all time. If he is more Pippen than Kobe, he's still in the same conversation.
quotes.quote: I'm not buying it because that's that's said in a in a way of Scottie Pippen is less than something. Scottie Pippen is a top-50 player of all time. If he is more Pippen than Kobe, he's still in the same conversation, in the same tier of players. Now, I don't know, obviously Kobe Bryant is Kobe Bryant, but we're not going to we're not going to dress this thing up as any type of disrespect towards Scottie Pippen at all, you know. So if he's trying to say, hey, it's some tier A1 guys and some tier AB guys, whatever, I I'm going to leave that up to Colin Cowherd to to defend on his own. But if Jayson Tatum is more Scottie Pippen than Kobe Bryant, then give me both. I I'm going to take it. Yeah, give me both of those guys. I I'm not buying that.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum is an incredible player in his own right
quotes.excerpt: I think Jayson Tatum is Jayson Tatum. He's an incredible player, he's a great player in this league.
quotes.quote: I'm not buying that either. One, I think Jayson Tatum is Jayson Tatum. He's an incredible player, he's a great player in this league. He's earned everything that comes his way. So, and and Scottie Pippen has done that and so has Kobe, so I don't understand the comparison in general. It has, yeah, I feel like he's trying to say he's not the main guy. Like he's he's he's robbing to a Batman is what he's trying to say and it's I mean, look, I disagree with that. We're going to always create headlines when it's something to talk about between the dynamic and him and Jaylen Brown. Those two guys are both champions, they're both superstars in this league and they've both shown that they're proven winners. So all the other extra shit, I'm more concerned about figuring out their dynamic and and and what the real thing was. I care more about that than trying to sit here and and diminish them as players or as individuals as teammates. Jayson Tatum is Jayson Tatum. He's great. He's still going to continue to be great. He's a champion, he's been the winner since he stepped foot in. I think he's in a category of his own and I and he deserves to stand on those 10 by himself. So that's how I feel about it.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown is one of the best two-way players in the league
quotes.excerpt: I'm buying that he's definitely the best two-way player in the league.
quotes.quote: I'm buying that he's definitely the best two-way player in the league. You know, usually we give that type of title to guys that play the two or they play the three and Jaylen Brown has has been exceptional on both ends of the floor, especially what he was able to do last year and how he's able to fit into what Philly is building right now. So I'm with Carmelo on this one. If Wemby didn't exist in this league, he would win defensive player of the year this season. Why not?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown is a top two-way player
quotes.excerpt: I agree as far as Jaylen Brown being one of the top two-way players in this league.
quotes.quote: I agree as far as Jaylen Brown being one of the top two-way players in this league. You know, think about guys like a healthy Kawhi, you can't overlook somebody like that. Um, but JB is up there for sure. Uh, as far as winning a DPOY, that's tough to say. It's harder for it's harder for guards to even win that award. So, Right. Yeah, I don't know about that part, but I agree he's good on the defensive end. Obviously he shows up every night on the offensive end. So, uh, it's not it's not far off.
